title: SepsisScreen
description: Shape contract for the sepsis-suspicion reasoning pass. Three echoed inputs, then the qSOFA screen result, then the justification for it. The input is a closed set of three numerics rather than a document, so unlike every other contract in this pack nothing here is copied out of prose.

x-notes.propertyOrder: LOAD-BEARING, as everywhere in this pack. The three qSOFA inputs (respiratory_rate, systolic_bp, gcs) are echoed FIRST because on this contract the echo is the reasoning: the screen is a lookup on those three numbers, so a model that has just written them down has everything the verdict requires. qsofa_score and positive follow immediately. The criteria_met array and screen_reason follow the verdict rather than preceding it, because 'which criteria support this' is a question about an answer that must already exist. assessment_confidence sits near the END for the reason it does in shock.schema.json.
x-notes.positiveIsABoolean: `positive` is a boolean, because qSOFA is a binary screen: a positive screen is any two of three criteria and there is no abstention to express — the tool that decides it always has an answer. Unlike shock_category there is no `indeterminate` member, because the medprotocol qsofa command returns an answer for every set of three inputs it is handed, so a model asked to report the screen has nothing legitimate to decline. What it CAN get wrong is reading the verdict or the criteria, and those are the axes this shape is built to expose.
x-notes.criteriaMetIsAnEnum: criteria_met holds CRITERION NAMES, not free prose, and the list is the closed three a qSOFA screen has. This is what makes the fidelity check exact: a criterion outside the list, or inside it but not met by this payload's numbers, is a model that re-derived the thresholds instead of reading the screen. The grammar cannot emit a name outside the enum, so the scorer catches the case that matters — a real criterion cited when the numbers do not meet it.
x-notes.reasonIsFreeText: screen_reason is a string rather than an enum. The criteria are closed; the model's narration is not, and a model that explains why it called the screen positive should be able to say so in its own words — that sentence is the most useful thing this contract can produce and an enum would delete it. It is consequently NOT graded automatically, which is stated here so nobody reads its presence as a checked field.
x-notes.numericBounds: minimum/maximum on the echoes and on assessment_confidence are documentation and validator input; llama.cpp's json-schema-to-grammar does not enforce numeric ranges in GBNF.

respiratory_rate.description: Respiratory rate in breaths per minute

positive.description: Whether the qSOFA screen is positive (two or more criteria met)

criteria_met.description: The qSOFA criteria this patient meets

screen_reason.description: A sentence explaining which criteria were met and what the screen means
